title: ScaGNN: a Graph Neural Network for Multiple Scattering Simulations
abstract: arXiv:2609.37509v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The boundary element method (BEM) provides an efficient numerical framework for solving multiple scattering problems in unbounded homogeneous domains. By restricting the discretization to the domain boundaries, it substantially reduces computational complexity. The procedure first consists in determining the solution trace on the boundaries of the domain by solving a boundary integral equation. Then, the volumetric solution can be recovered at low computational cost using a boundary integral representation. As the first step of the BEM represents the main computational bottleneck, we present ScaGNN, a learning-based approach designed to approximate the solution trace. It relies on a graph neural network architecture that incorporates a dynamic adaptive edge sampling mechanism for selecting the most relevant interactions to model. translated_title: ScaGNN：一种用于多重散射模拟的图神经网络
translated_abstract: 边界元方法（BEM）为求解无界均匀域中的多重散射问题提供了一种高效的数值框架。通过将离散化限制在域的边界上，它显著降低了计算复杂度。该过程首先通过求解边界积分方程来确定域边界上的解迹，然后可以利用边界积分表示以较低的计算成本恢复体积解。由于BEM的第一步是主要的计算瓶颈，我们提出了ScaGNN，这是一种旨在近似求解解迹的基于学习的方法。它依赖于一种图神经网络架构，该架构结合了动态自适应边采样机制，用于选择最相关的相互作用进行建模。在预期误差和边长的中间预测的引导下，该机制在各个阶段……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: ScaGNN提出了一种结合动态自适应边采样机制的图神经网络，通过近似边界上的解迹来加速边界元方法求解多重散射问题时的主要计算瓶颈。
en_tdlr: ScaGNN is a graph neural network with a dynamic adaptive edge sampling mechanism that accelerates the main computational bottleneck of the boundary element method for multiple scattering simulations by approximating the solution trace on domain boundaries.
